title: Is Salary Sacrifice Worth It? A Guide to Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Wondering if salary sacrifice is worth it? Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, understand tax, super, and state differences in ordinary-time earnings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or are considering a salary offer, understanding how to convert your pay to an annual figure is essential. The basic formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you your gross annual income before tax, super, and any deductions. It assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For a 38-hour week, that is (hourly rate × 38) × 2. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

## Understanding Minimum and Award Rates

Australia has a National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

However, many employees are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. Award rates vary by job type and experience level. Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement for your correct base rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate should not already include the 25% casual loading. When using a calculator, you typically enter the base rate and then add the loading separately. This ensures you see the correct total.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Average weekly ordinary-time earnings vary across Australian states and territories. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), the national average for full-time adult ordinary-time earnings was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. However, states like New South Wales and Victoria tend to have higher averages, while Tasmania and South Australia are often lower. These differences reflect industry mix, cost of living, and labour market conditions.

When comparing a salary offer or your own hourly rate, it is useful to know the average for your state. The ABS publishes detailed data by state and territory. Keep in mind that these are averages, not medians for a specific job. Your actual pay may differ based on your role, experience, and employer.

## Tax and Superannuation

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. Tax and the Medicare levy are deducted by your employer under the PAYG system. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). These rates apply to your taxable income after any deductions or salary sacrifice arrangements.

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if you earn $100,000, your employer contributes $12,000 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

## Is Salary Sacrifice Worth It?

Salary sacrifice (also called salary packaging) allows you to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower the tax you pay. However, it also reduces the base on which your super guarantee is calculated (since super is based on ordinary earnings, which are reduced by the sacrificed amount).

So, is salary sacrifice worth it? It depends on your individual circumstances. If you are in a higher tax bracket, sacrificing into super or a novated lease can save you money. But for lower-income earners, the benefit may be minimal. Also, some salary sacrifice arrangements have caps and fees. Always consult a tax professional and consider your long-term goals. The Australian Taxation Office provides guidelines on what can be sacrificed.

For a quick estimate of your take-home pay, you can use [the timesheet](/). It calculates annual gross, super, and tax based on your hourly rate and hours. You can also explore [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to understand how salary sacrifice affects your retirement savings.

## Important Notes

This article provides estimates only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming consistent hours and no unpaid overtime. Tax estimates use the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. No HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging deductions are included. For a precise determination of your pay, speak to your employer or a qualified accountant.
